description: The bar chart illustrates the effect of context masking perturbations on various linguistic tags—case, gender, number, and tense—across different multilingual BERT models (mBERT-L2, XLM-L2, mBERT-R2, XLM-R2, mBERT-B2, and XLM-B2). The vertical axis represents the effect, with values ranging from approximately -2 to 20, and error bars indicate the standard deviation. For the 'case' tag, mBERT-B2 shows the highest effect (around 12), followed by XLM-B2 (around 11), while mBERT-L2 has a moderate effect (around 6). For 'gender', mBERT-B2 again shows the highest effect (around 4), followed by XLM-B2 (around 3), with mBERT-L2 showing a lower effect (around 1). In the 'number' category, mBERT-B2 has the highest effect (around 3), followed by XLM-B2 (around 2), with mBERT-L2 showing a lower effect (around 1). For the 'tense' tag, all models show very small effects, with mBERT-B2 having a slightly positive effect (around 0.5), XLM-B2 showing a negative effect (around -0.5), and the other models showing effects close to zero. The chart demonstrates that the impact of context masking perturbations varies significantly across tags and models, with mBERT-B2 and XLM-B2 generally showing higher effects compared to the other models.
